scenes.title: Spotting Names Around Us
narration: Look around your classroom! Do you see a table, a chair, or a friendly teacher?
Everything you see has a name, and we call these special words nouns.
But did you know there are two main types of nouns?

scenes.title: Common Nouns Explained
narration: Common nouns are general names for people, places, or things.
If you say boy, city, or dog, those are common nouns.
They do not need a capital letter unless they start a sentence.

scenes.title: Proper Nouns Are Special
narration: Proper nouns are the special names for one specific person, place, or thing.
Like your own name, Aarav, or our beautiful country, India.
These nouns always start with a big capital letter!

scenes.title: Let Us Recap Together
narration: Remember, common nouns are general, but proper nouns are specific and special.
Always use a capital letter for a proper noun to show it is unique.
Can you write your own name and your city's name today?

scenes.title: What Are Nouns
narration: Look around your room, what do you see?
Everything you see has a name.
These naming words are called nouns.

scenes.title: Types Of Nouns
narration: Nouns can be a person like a teacher.
Nouns can be a place like a park.
Nouns can be a thing like a ball.
Nouns can be an animal like a cat.

scenes.title: Example In Sentences
narration: Let us read this sentence together.
Rohan eats a sweet mango.
Rohan is the person noun here.
Mango is the thing noun here.

scenes.title: Wrap Up And Practice
narration: Nouns are names for people, places, things, or animals.
You use nouns every single day.
Think about it, can you name three nouns in your kitchen?

scenes.title: Meet The Name Replacers
narration: Have you ever talked about your friend Rohan without saying his name over and over?
We use special helper words called pronouns to make talking much easier.
Let us see how these magic words work.

scenes.title: Using He and She
narration: When we talk about a boy like Rohan, we say he.
Rohan likes cricket so he plays every day.
When we talk about a girl like Priya, we say she.
Priya loves books so she reads often.

scenes.title: It and They
narration: If you talk about a school bag, use the word it.
The red bag is heavy because it is full.
When there is a group of friends, we use they.
Priya and Rohan are happy because they are playing.

scenes.title: Recap and Try
narration: We use he for boys, she for girls, it for things, and they for groups.
These words help us speak faster and clearer every single day.
Think about it: what pronoun would you use if you were talking about your teacher?

scenes.title: Spotting the Difference
narration: Look at your pencil case on your desk.
Now count your crayons in the box.
How do we talk about one versus many?

scenes.title: The Magic S Rule
narration: When there is only one thing, it is singular.
When there are two or more, we add an s.
One apple becomes two apples for us.
The s shows us there is a group.

scenes.title: Practice at the Market
narration: Rohan goes to the market to buy fruit.
He picks up one orange from a crate.
Then he buys five sweet oranges for home.
We say orange for one and oranges for many.

scenes.title: Remembering the Rules
narration: Singular means just one object or person.
Plural means more than one, usually adding s.
Can you name three things in your bag?

scenes.title: What are describing words?
narration: Look at your school bag, is it big or small?
Words that tell us more about things are called adjectives.
They help us paint a clear picture with our words.

scenes.title: How adjectives work
narration: An adjective usually comes before the noun.
Instead of just saying apple, you can say red apple.
These words describe color, size, or shape.
They help others see exactly what you see.

scenes.title: Let us describe lunch
narration: Rohan has a yummy samosa for lunch.
Yummy is the adjective describing the samosa.
He also has a crunchy apple.
Crunchy tells us how the apple feels.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: Adjectives describe nouns like people, places, or things.
They tell us about size, color, and feelings.
Think about it, what two adjectives would you use to describe your favorite toy?

scenes.title: Spotting Objects at Home
narration: Look at these things on Rohan's study desk.
Do you say a book or an book?
Let's find out how to choose the right word.

scenes.title: The Rule of Five
narration: English has five special letters called vowels.
If a word starts with these, we use an.
For all other letters, we use a.

scenes.title: Practice with Rohan
narration: Rohan has an apple for his snack.
He also has a sharp pencil.
See how the first letter changes the word?

scenes.title: Time to Recap
narration: Use an for vowels and a for everything else.
You are now a grammar superstar.
Think about it: would you say a orange or an orange?

scenes.title: Spotting Actions at Home
narration: Have you noticed how much you do in one day?
You jump, you eat, and you play with toys.
These special words are called verbs.

scenes.title: What are Verbs?
narration: A verb is a word that shows action.
If you can do it, it is a verb.
Let us look at some common action words.

scenes.title: Seeing Verbs in Action
narration: Rohan runs in the park.
The word runs is the verb here.
Priya eats a sweet mango.
The word eats is the action word.

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Verbs are action words we use every day.
They tell us what someone is doing.
Can you name three verbs you did today?

scenes.title: Where Is Rohan's Toy?
narration: Rohan is looking for his favorite teddy bear in his room.
Can you help him find where the toy is hiding?
We use special words called prepositions to show location.

scenes.title: Learning New Position Words
narration: The bear is in the box.
Now, the bear is on the chair.
Look, the bear is under the bed.
Prepositions tell us where things are placed.

scenes.title: Finding Rohan's Toy
narration: Rohan checks the desk and sees the bear is next to his book.
He looks behind the door, but it is not there.
Finally, he finds it between the two pillows.

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: We learned words like in, on, under, and between today.
These words help us describe where objects are located.
Think about it: where is your school bag right now?

scenes.title: What do you own
narration: Do you have a pencil or a bag in your school bag today?
We use special words to tell others what we own.
Let's learn how to use has and have correctly.

scenes.title: When to use have
narration: We use have with I and you.
We also use have for plural groups like they or we.
Example: I have two shiny red apples.

scenes.title: When to use has
narration: Use has when talking about just one person.
Rohan is one boy, so Rohan has a bat.
My cat is also one, so she has a ball.

scenes.title: Quick review
narration: Remember, I and you always take have.
He, she, and it always take has.
Think about it: What toy has your best friend brought to school?

scenes.title: Spotting the Past Tense
narration: Have you ever told a story about what happened yesterday?
When we talk about the past, we use special helper words.
Today we will learn how to use was and were.

scenes.title: When to use Was
narration: Use was for one person or one thing.
I was at the park.
He was happy.
The cat was hungry.

scenes.title: When to use Were
narration: Use were for more than one person or thing.
They were playing cricket.
We were at school.
Riya and Rahul were friends.

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Was is for one, and were is for many.
You did a great job learning these words today.
Think about it: Can you write a sentence about how you were feeling yesterday?

scenes.title: Meet Your New Friends
narration: Have you noticed how we talk about ourselves and others?
We use special helper words to connect our sentences.
Today, let's learn about is, am, and are.

scenes.title: The Magic Helper Rules
narration: Use am only when you talk about yourself.
Use is for one person or one thing.
Use are for many people or things.
Are also works when you talk to someone else.

scenes.title: Let Us Practice Together
narration: I am eating a tasty mango.
Rohan is my best friend.
They are playing in the park.
You are a very smart student.

scenes.title: Remember and Try
narration: Remember, am is for I, is for one, and are for many.
These words make our sentences clear and happy.
Think about it: what would you say to describe your family?

scenes.title: The Magic Connector
narration: Have you ever wanted to join two sentences into one super sentence?
Meet the special words called conjunctions that help us do just that.
Today, we will learn about the word and.

scenes.title: Using The Word And
narration: We use and to add things together.
Imagine you have a red balloon and a blue balloon.
Instead of two sentences, you can say I have a red balloon and a blue balloon.
It makes our talking sound much smoother.

scenes.title: Rohan's Snack Time
narration: Rohan is hungry at his school in Delhi.
He has a sweet mango in his bag.
He also has a crunchy paratha.
He eats a mango and a paratha.

scenes.title: Time To Review
narration: Conjunctions are linking words that join ideas.
We used and to put two things together today.
Think about it, what two fruits would you like to eat and share?

scenes.title: Who is in your family?
narration: Do you live with your parents and siblings at home?
Let us learn the special names we use for family members.
Meet Rohan, who is showing us his happy family today.

scenes.title: Names for family members
narration: Rohan calls the man who takes care of him Father.
He calls the kind woman who loves him Mother.
Rohan has a sister who is his best friend.
He also has a brother who plays cricket with him.

scenes.title: Extended family members
narration: Rohan visits his grandparents who live in a big house.
The father of his father is his Grandfather.
The mother of his mother is his Grandmother.
Rohan loves to eat yummy snacks with his cousins too.

scenes.title: Recap and thinking
narration: We learned father, mother, sister, brother, and grandparents.
Using the right names helps us talk about our loved ones.
Think about it: who is the youngest person in your family?

scenes.title: What Happened Before
narration: Do you remember what you did yesterday after school?
When we talk about finished actions, we change our verbs.
We usually add the letters e-d to the end.

scenes.title: How We Change Words
narration: If you play today, you played yesterday.
If you jump today, you jumped yesterday.
Just add e-d to show the time has passed.

scenes.title: A Story About Rohan
narration: Rohan likes to cook yummy food.
Yesterday, Rohan cooked a big dinner.
He also helped his mother clean up.

scenes.title: Let Us Remember
narration: Use e-d for things finished in the past.
Now you try, what did you eat for lunch?

scenes.title: What Do You Do Daily
narration: Look at your friend Rohan in the park today.
Do you notice what he does every single morning?
He plays football to stay healthy and strong.

scenes.title: Learning the Simple Present Rule
narration: When we talk about habits, we use the simple present tense.
If the person is one, like he or she, we add s.
Example: Rohan runs fast on the grassy field.
But if we say I or they, we do not add s.

scenes.title: Let Us Practice Together
narration: Look at Priya, our classmate who loves books.
Does she read a book or reads a book?
Since Priya is one person, she reads a book.
Great job, you are learning fast today.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Use the simple present for habits and things that stay true.
Remember to add s for he, she, or a single name.
Think about it: What is one thing you do every morning?

scenes.title: The Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered how we tell stories or ask questions?
Every sentence we say has a special job to do.
Let us learn the three main types of sentences today!

scenes.title: Three Types of Sentences
narration: First, a statement tells us a fact like, I like mangoes.
Second, a question asks something, like, Where is my ball?
Third, a command tells someone to do something, like, Clean up!

scenes.title: Let Us Practice Together
narration: Rohan says, The sun is hot. This is a statement.
Rohan asks, Is it raining? This is a question.
Rohan says, Drink your water! This is a command.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, statements tell, questions ask, and commands give orders.
Look for the period, question mark, or exclamation point at the end.
Think about it, what sentence type would you use to ask for help?

scenes.title: Meet Our Animal Friends
narration: Have you ever visited a zoo in India or seen a pet at home?
Animals are everywhere, but do you know their special names?
Let us learn some new words to describe our furry friends today.

scenes.title: Learning Animal Groups
narration: Some animals are big, like this tall elephant.
Some animals are small, like this cute rabbit.
Others can fly high, like a colorful parrot.
And some swim in the river, like a funny fish.

scenes.title: Practice With Words
narration: Look at the cat. Can you say cat?
Now look at the dog. Dog starts with a D.
This is a cow. It gives us milk.
And this is a lion. It has a big mane.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: We learned words for big, small, flying, and swimming animals.
Using good words helps us tell stories about animals.
Think about it: What is your favorite animal and why?

scenes.title: Welcome to School
narration: Do you like going to school every day with your friends?
Let us learn the names of things we use in class.
Look at your bag, what do you see inside it?

scenes.title: Tools for Learning
narration: This is a pencil used for writing your letters.
We use a sharpener to make the pencil tip pointy.
An eraser helps us fix any mistakes we make.
We keep our books in a sturdy school bag.

scenes.title: Classroom Objects
narration: A teacher writes notes on the white board.
You sit on a wooden chair at your desk.
We use a scale to draw straight lines.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Remember, we use a pencil, eraser, and scale.
Everything in our classroom helps us learn new things.
Think about it: which item is your favorite to use?

scenes.title: What do you see outside?
narration: Look out your window at the park, what do you see?
The world around us is full of amazing things.
Let us learn some new words for nature today.

scenes.title: Learning Nature Words
narration: The big green plant with a trunk is a tree.
The bright yellow flower in the garden is a bloom.
The big blue space above us is the sky.
The water flowing in the river is cool.

scenes.title: Let us use our words
narration: Look at this tree in the park, it is tall.
See the bright bloom, it is pretty.
The sky is blue and the river is wide.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: We learned tree, bloom, sky, and river today.
Using words helps us describe the world.
Can you name one more thing in nature?

scenes.title: Who Helps Us Daily
narration: Look around your neighborhood, who do you see helping us every day?
A community is a group of people living and working in one place.
Let us learn the special names for these helpful people.

scenes.title: Meet The Helpers
narration: The person who keeps us safe is a police officer.
When we feel sick, we visit a doctor.
A person who brings letters is a postman.
The person who teaches us at school is a teacher.

scenes.title: A Day In Delhi
narration: Imagine we are in a busy market in Delhi.
Rohan buys fresh bread from the baker.
His sister pays the shopkeeper five rupees.
They wave hello to the friendly gardener.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Community members are people who live and work together near us.
Learning these words helps us describe our world clearly.
Think about it: who is one helper you saw in your street today?

scenes.title: Notice Your Feelings
narration: Have you ever felt super happy or maybe a little bit sad?
We have many feelings inside us every single day.
Let us learn the words to describe how we feel.

scenes.title: Learning New Words
narration: When you win a game, you feel happy.
When you lose a toy, you feel sad.
When you see a big dog, you might feel scared.
When you learn something new, you feel excited.

scenes.title: A Day With Rohan
narration: Rohan got a yummy laddo for his snack.
He felt very happy eating it.
Then he dropped his pencil and felt frustrated.
His friend helped him, so he felt thankful.

scenes.title: Summary And Reflection
narration: We learned words like happy, sad, scared, and excited.
It is okay to have all these different feelings.
Think about it: how are you feeling right now?

scenes.title: What is for lunch?
narration: Have you ever wondered what your favorite lunch is called in English?
Let us learn some yummy food words together today.
Look at these colorful snacks on the table.

scenes.title: Learning new food words
narration: First is fruit, like a sweet red apple.
Next is a crunchy carrot from the garden.
Then we have warm, fluffy rice in a bowl.
And finally, a glass of cold milk.

scenes.title: Making a healthy plate
narration: Let us build a plate for Rohan.
Put the yellow banana on the plate.
Now add the green peas to his lunch.
Finally, add the tasty bread slice.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: We learned words like apple, carrot, rice, and milk.
Remember to say the name of your food clearly.
Think about it: what is the very first thing you eat for breakfast?

scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered what people do for work in our neighborhood?
Every job has a special name, like a doctor or a baker.
Let us learn some new words for these cool jobs today!

scenes.title: Learning New Job Words
narration: A person who grows food on a farm is a farmer.
A person who teaches in a classroom is a teacher.
A person who fixes your teeth is a dentist.
A person who flies an airplane is a pilot.

scenes.title: Meet Rohan's Community
narration: Rohan visits the market where his friend Priya sells fruits.
Then, he sees Ravi the police officer keeping the street safe.
Finally, he visits Dr. Maya at the clinic for a checkup.

scenes.title: Putting It All Together
narration: We learned that different jobs have different names.
Remember to use these names when you talk about your community.
Think about it: what job would you like to do when you grow up?

scenes.title: What's Your Ride?
narration: Have you ever wondered how we travel to school or the market?
We use many different types of transport to go places.
Let us learn the special names for these cool machines.

scenes.title: Words For Travel
narration: A car has four wheels and carries a small family.
A big bus carries many people to school together.
A bicycle is a fun way to ride in the park.
A train travels fast on long metal tracks.

scenes.title: A Trip In India
narration: Imagine you are taking a trip across India.
First, you ride a rickshaw to the busy station.
Then, you hop on a train to see the green fields.
Finally, an airplane flies high above the white clouds.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: We learned words like car, bus, train, and plane.
Remember, transport helps us reach our destination quickly.
Think about it: If you could ride any vehicle today, which one would you pick?

scenes.title: What Is A Story
narration: Do you love listening to bedtime stories about brave heroes?
A story is just a fun way to share an adventure.
Every story has a beginning, a middle, and an end.

scenes.title: Parts Of A Story
narration: The beginning introduces our friend, like Ravi the boy.
The middle tells us about a big problem or challenge.
The end shows us how he solves the problem happily.

scenes.title: Ravi Finds A Key
narration: Ravi found a shiny gold key in his garden.
He looked for the box that the key could open.
He found a wooden chest and opened it with joy.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Stories need a character, a problem, and a solution.
Reading stories helps us learn new words and ideas.
Think about it: What is your favorite story book?

scenes.title: The Big Discovery
narration: Look at your bag. Is it heavy or is it light today?
We use words that mean the exact opposite to describe things.
These special pairs of words are called antonyms.

scenes.title: How Antonyms Work
narration: An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word.
Think of day and night, they are completely different.
If you are not hot, you are cold.

scenes.title: A Day with Antonyms
narration: Rohan ate a big apple for his snack.
Then he found a small seed inside it.
Big and small are antonyms that describe size.
The sun was high up, not low down.

scenes.title: Let Us Recap
narration: Antonyms are pairs of words with opposite meanings.
They help us describe how things are different.
Can you think of the opposite of the word happy?

scenes.title: Spotting Differences Everywhere
narration: Have you ever noticed how some things are just the complete opposite of others?
Look at your school bag, is it heavy or is it light today?
Today, we will learn words that mean the exact opposite of each other!

scenes.title: Understanding How Opposites Work
narration: An opposite word is like a mirror image that tells us the other side.
If a dosa is hot, the opposite is a cold glass of lassi.
Big things have a small partner, just like an elephant and a mouse.

scenes.title: Using Opposites in Sentences
narration: Let us try a sentence with Rohan who is a fast runner.
But his friend Meera is a slow walker.
See how fast and slow show us the difference?

scenes.title: Quick Recap and Practice
narration: We learned that opposites help us describe the world in a fun way.
Remember, happy and sad or tall and short are all great examples.
Think about it: what is the opposite of the word clean?

scenes.title: Finding New Words Together
narration: Have you ever felt very happy at a birthday party?
You could say you are happy, or you could say you are glad!
Words that mean the same are called synonyms.

scenes.title: Learning Our Synonyms
narration: A synonym is just a different word for the same thing.
Think of it like wearing different shirts, but it is still you!
Using synonyms makes our writing much more exciting.

scenes.title: Fun With Examples
narration: Look at the word big. We can also say large.
If a dog is fast, we can also say it is quick.
If a room is small, we can also say it is tiny.

scenes.title: Recap And Practice
narration: Synonyms are words that have the same meaning.
They help us describe things in brand new ways.
Can you think of a synonym for the word sad?

scenes.title: What is the Story About?
narration: Have you ever wondered what a whole story is mostly about?
Every story has a main idea, like the heart of the book.
It tells us the most important thing happening on the page.

scenes.title: Clues to Help You
narration: Look at the title first, it is a big clue for you.
Next, look at the pictures to see what they show.
Finally, ask yourself what the story is talking about most.

scenes.title: A Story About Rohan
narration: Rohan plays cricket, Rohan eats mangoes, and Rohan runs fast.
The sentences all talk about what Rohan does all day.
So, the main idea is: Rohan is a busy boy.

scenes.title: Remember the Main Idea
narration: Remember, the main idea is what the whole thing is about.
Don't let the small details distract you from the big picture.
What is the main idea of your favorite story tonight?

scenes.title: What is a Poem?
narration: Have you ever heard words that sound like music?
Poems use special words to paint a picture in your mind.
Many poems have words that end with the same sound.

scenes.title: Rhyming Words Together
narration: Rhyming words are like a happy pair of friends.
Listen to these two words: cat and hat.
They both end with the same sound, so they rhyme!
Can you hear how they sound just like each other?

scenes.title: Reading a Short Poem
narration: Let us read this little poem about a mouse.
The mouse lives inside a tiny house.
He runs around and stays as quiet as a grouse.
Mouse, house, and grouse all rhyme at the end!

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Poems use rhythm and rhyming words to sound fun.
Look for rhyming words at the end of each line.
Think about it: what word rhymes with star?

scenes.title: Meeting at the Park
narration: Have you ever wondered how to write down two friends talking?
When Arjun speaks to Priya, we use special marks called quotation marks.
These marks look like tiny commas hugging the words they say.

scenes.title: Learning the Rules
narration: First, put the talking marks around the words said out loud.
Start the sentence inside the marks with a capital letter.
Add a comma, question mark, or exclamation point before the closing mark.
Always say who is speaking after the sentence finishes.

scenes.title: Writing a Dialogue
narration: Let us write: Arjun asked, Where is the ball?
We write it as: Arjun asked, “Where is the ball?”
See how the question mark stays safely inside the hug?

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Remember to use quotation marks for words spoken aloud.
Keep the punctuation marks inside those special hugs.
Think about it: How would you write a dialogue between you and your teacher?

scenes.title: The Reading Mystery
narration: Have you ever read a story and wondered what happened next?
Reading is like being a detective looking for clues in a book.
Today, we learn how to find the secret meaning in sentences.

scenes.title: Finding The Clues
narration: First, we look for the main character in the story.
Next, we find out where they are and what they are doing.
Ask yourself, who is this about and what did they do?
These clues help us understand the whole story better.

scenes.title: A Story About Ravi
narration: Let us read about Ravi. Ravi eats a red apple.
We see the word apple starts with the letter a.
Because apple starts with a sound, we say an apple.
Ravi is happy because he loves his healthy snack.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Remember to look for characters and what they do in sentences.
Always check if your words follow the right rules.
Think about it: What is your favorite book character and why?

scenes.title: The Story Detective Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered how to find answers inside your favorite storybooks?
When we read, we look for clues just like a real detective.
Let us practice finding answers together today.

scenes.title: The Three Step Rule
narration: First, read the question carefully to see what it asks.
Second, scan the text for special words from the question.
Third, read the sentence around those words to find the answer.

scenes.title: Solving a Story Example
narration: Rohan ate a juicy mango at the park today.
Question: What did Rohan eat at the park?
Look for the word Rohan and the word park in the story.
We see he ate a mango, so that is our answer.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, read the question, scan the text, and find the answer.
You are now ready to be a story detective every single day.
Think about it: Can you find the name of the main character in your next book?

scenes.title: The First Step
narration: Have you ever made a yummy vegetable sandwich for lunch?
To make it, we must follow steps in the right order.
Today we will learn how to sequence events in a story.

scenes.title: What Is Sequencing
narration: Sequencing means putting parts of a story in the right order.
We look for words like first, next, and then.
These words tell us what happened at the start and end.
If we mix them up, the story gets very silly!

scenes.title: A Day With Rohan
narration: First, Rohan wakes up and brushes his teeth.
Next, he puts on his uniform and eats breakfast.
Then, he walks to his school in Delhi.
Finally, he learns his lessons in class.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Remember, always look for the order of events.
Using clue words like first and then helps a lot.
Think about it: what is the very first thing you do when you get home?

scenes.title: The Hook
narration: Have you ever wanted to tell a story about your favourite day?
To write it well, we need to group our sentences together.
A group of sentences about one topic is called a paragraph.

scenes.title: The Idea
narration: Start with a topic sentence that tells us what you are writing about.
Then add a few sentences with extra details to explain more.
Finally, end with a closing sentence to wrap everything up neatly.

scenes.title: A Tasty Example
narration: Let us write about a mango. My topic sentence is: I love eating mangoes.
Now the details: They are very sweet and bright yellow.
The closing sentence: Mango is the best fruit in summer.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, a paragraph has a topic, details, and a closing sentence.
Keep all your sentences focused on just one big idea.
Think about it: What is one thing you would like to write a paragraph about today?

scenes.title: What is a sentence
narration: Have you ever tried to share a big idea with your friends?
To speak clearly, we need to put our words in a special order.
A sentence is a group of words that tells a complete thought.

scenes.title: The Sentence Rules
narration: Every sentence must start with a big capital letter.
It also needs a naming part and an action part.
And don't forget the tiny dot called a full stop at the end!

scenes.title: Let's build a sentence
narration: Let's write about Rohan eating a yummy mango.
First, capital R for Rohan.
Next, add the action: eats a mango.
Finally, add a full stop: Rohan eats a mango.

scenes.title: Time to recap
narration: Remember, sentences start with capitals and end with a full stop.
They must have a complete thought to make sense.
Think about it: can you write a sentence about your favorite toy?

scenes.title: Sending a Special Message
narration: Have you ever wanted to send a message to a friend far away?
A letter is a wonderful way to talk to someone you love.
Let's learn how to write one to your friend, Rohan.

scenes.title: The Parts of a Letter
narration: First, write the date at the top so Rohan knows when you wrote it.
Next, write a greeting like Dear Rohan to say hello.
Then, write your message using short, simple sentences.
Finally, add a closing like Love or Your friend.

scenes.title: Writing Our Letter
narration: Start with the date: 15 August.
Write Dear Rohan at the top.
Write I like school, it is fun.
Finish with Love, Ananya.

scenes.title: Time to Mail It
narration: Remember to write the date, a greeting, your message, and a closing.
Now put it in an envelope and add a stamp.
Think about it: Who would you like to write a letter to today?

scenes.title: The Mystery Beginning
narration: Have you ever started a story but did not know how to end it?
Let us look at a story about Rohan and his lost ball.
Rohan is playing in his garden when his ball rolls into a bush.

scenes.title: Building Your Plot
narration: To finish, first decide what happens next to solve the problem.
Maybe Rohan looks behind the leaves and finds a hidden puppy.
The puppy was hiding with the ball!
Always make sure your ending matches the start of your story.

scenes.title: Writing the Ending
narration: Now, use a clear sentence to finish your tale.
Rohan smiled, picked up his ball, and played with his new friend.
See? Rohan is happy and the story is complete.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember to solve the problem and give your character a happy finish.
Good stories always have a clear beginning, middle, and end.
Think about it: If a cat climbed a tree, how would you finish that story?

scenes.title: Who Are You
narration: Have you ever wanted to tell a new friend all about yourself?
We use personal information to share our name and age.
Let's learn how to write these facts down!

scenes.title: Writing Your Details
narration: First, write your full name starting with capital letters.
Next, write your age using a number like 7.
Always use a full sentence to describe yourself.
A sentence always ends with a little dot called a period.

scenes.title: Meet Rohan
narration: Let us practice with our friend Rohan from Delhi.
He writes, My name is Rohan.
Then he adds, I am 8 years old.

scenes.title: Quick Review
narration: Remember to use capitals for names and periods for endings.
Writing your details clearly helps people get to know you.
Think about it: What are three things you would tell a new friend?

scenes.title: Look at the Picture
narration: Have you ever looked at a photo and wanted to tell a story about it?
Today we will learn how to describe pictures using our words.
First, look closely at who is in the picture.

scenes.title: What Do You See
narration: Look for the main action happening in the scene.
Next, describe where the people or things are.
Try to use words about colors or sizes too.
Remember to use a capital letter at the start of your sentence.

scenes.title: An Example for You
narration: Let us look at a picture of Rohan playing in a park.
We can say, Rohan kicks the red ball.
We can add, He is very happy today.
Every sentence ends with a full stop.

scenes.title: Time to Practice
narration: To describe a picture, find who, where, and what they do.
Use short, clear sentences to tell your story.
Think about it: what would you say about a picture of your family?

scenes.title: Hook: Starting Your Story
narration: Have you ever wanted to write a fun story about your day?
Let us learn how to write sentences that make sense.
First, think about what you want to say.

scenes.title: The Idea: Sentence Steps
narration: Every good sentence needs a naming word and a doing word.
For example, Ravi runs fast in the park.
Always start with a capital letter.
And finish with a tiny dot called a full stop.

scenes.title: Example: Building a Story
narration: Let us write about Meera eating a mango.
Step one, write Meera with a big M.
Step two, add eats a mango.
Step three, put a full stop at the end.

scenes.title: Recap: You Are An Author
narration: Remember to use capital letters and full stops.
Small steps make your writing easy to read.
Think about it: What story will you write today?

scenes.title: Meeting New Friends
narration: Have you ever met someone new at the playground or school?
Do you feel shy when you want to say hello?
Today we will learn how to introduce ourselves easily!

scenes.title: The Simple Steps
narration: First, say a friendly greeting like hello.
Next, tell them your name clearly.
Then, share one fun fact about yourself.
Finally, ask their name to start a conversation.

scenes.title: A Friendly Example
narration: Imagine meeting a friend named Priya.
Say, Hello, I am Aarav.
I love to play cricket.
What is your name?

scenes.title: Time to Practice
narration: Remember, always smile and speak clearly.
Greeting, name, and a hobby make a great introduction.
Think about it: What is one fun thing you will tell a new friend today?

scenes.title: The Curious Question Game
narration: Have you ever wanted to learn something new about your friend at school?
We use special words to ask questions, like Who, What, Where, and When.
Asking questions is the best way to start a fun conversation!

scenes.title: How to Ask Questions
narration: To ask a question, start with a question word and add a question mark.
For example, you can ask, What is your favorite snack?
Always remember to use your friendly voice so people know you are curious.

scenes.title: Answering Like a Pro
narration: When someone asks you a question, listen carefully to the first word.
If I ask, Where do you live?, you answer with a place.
You could say, I live in Delhi, or I live in Mumbai.
A good answer is clear and matches the question asked.

scenes.title: Recap and Try It
narration: Remember to use question words and always add a question mark.
Listen to the question first, then give a clear and polite answer.
Think about it: What question will you ask your friend today?

scenes.title: Spotting the Details
narration: Have you ever tried to describe your best friend or favorite toy?
We use special words called adjectives to tell others what we see.
They help our friends picture exactly what we are talking about.

scenes.title: How We Describe
narration: First, think about the size, like saying big or small.
Next, talk about the color, like bright red or deep blue.
Finally, share how something feels, like soft or bumpy.

scenes.title: Anjali at the Park
narration: Let us describe Anjali's shiny, yellow bicycle at the park.
We can say, 'She has a fast, yellow bike.'
Or look at her soft, blue scarf fluttering in the wind.

scenes.title: Time to Practice
narration: Remember, start with the size, color, or how it feels.
Using these words makes your stories much more fun to hear.
Think about it: Can you describe your favorite school bag in three words?

scenes.title: What is Role-Play?
narration: Have you ever pretended to be a teacher or a doctor at home?
Acting like someone else is called role-play.
It is like being an actor in a play!

scenes.title: Using Your Voice
narration: When you role-play, you must change your voice.
Speak loudly if you are a brave lion.
Whisper softly if you are a tiny mouse.
Use your face to show feelings too.

scenes.title: A Shopkeeper Example
narration: Let us pretend to buy apples at a shop.
Aarav says, May I have two apples please?
The shopkeeper says, Here you go, that is ten rupees.
Aarav replies, Thank you very much!

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Remember to use your acting voice and feelings.
Always be polite when you talk to others.
Think about it: Who would you like to pretend to be today?

scenes.title: Meeting a New Friend
narration: Have you ever wanted to say hello to a new friend at the park?
The best way to start is with a big, friendly smile.
Just say, Hello, my name is Rohan, what is your name?

scenes.title: Using Polite Words
narration: To be polite, we use special magic words.
When you need help, always say, Please.
When someone gives you a gift, say, Thank you.
If you bump into someone, say, I am sorry.

scenes.title: Asking for What You Need
narration: Let us practice asking for a book at the library.
Look at the person and speak in a clear voice.
Say, May I please borrow this book?

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Remember to smile, use polite words, and speak clearly.
Practice makes your conversation skills grow stronger every day.
Think about it: Who will you practice your new polite words with today?
